_doc: The vision and AR-development pop-ups (docs/vision-popups.md, docs/popups.md): one entry per tool of services/vision-popups, all in the one container on skippy-pc's GPU. vram_gb and est_seconds are bench.py's numbers (cold: weights loaded on the call).

popups.name: remove_background

output.description: cutout = the subject on transparency (PNG, the default); on_black = the subject on pure #000000, which is see-through on the Captain's Viture XR glasses (AR art); mask = the matte alone; json = coverage and the subject's box.

background.description: Which pictures to make (both by default).

lift.description: For on_black: raise the subject's darkest pixels by this much so they don't vanish on the glasses (0 = exact colours).

model.description: birefnet (default, crisp edges, best on ordinary photos); birefnet_matting for soft hair, fur and see-through edges.

popups.description: Cut the subject out of an attached picture (BiRefNet): a transparent PNG, or the subject on pure black, which the Captain's Viture XR glasses show as see-through, for AR art. Use when someone asks to remove or replace a background, make a sticker or cut-out, or prepare art for the glasses.

popups.name: upscale_image
popups.description: Make an attached picture four times bigger and sharper (Real-ESRGAN x4), up to 4096 pixels on the long side; a transparent picture keeps its transparency. Use when someone asks to upscale, enlarge, sharpen or increase the resolution of a picture.

popups.name: depth_map

output.description: depth = 8-bit greyscale, near is bright (default); depth16 = 16-bit for precise use; normals = a normal map (RGB = XYZ) for lighting; json = notes.

strength.description: How strongly depth bends the normal map (4 by default).

popups.description: A depth map of an attached picture (Depth Anything V2: relative, near is bright) or a normal map made from it, for AR occlusion, parallax and relighting. Use when the Captain asks for depth, a depth map, a normal map, or how far things are in a picture (relative, not metres).

popups.name: segment_image

text.description: What to cut out, in words ("the mug"): Grounding DINO finds it, SAM 2.1 traces it.

point.description: [x, y] in the picture's pixels on the thing to cut out.

box.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in pixels around the thing.

output.description: cutout (default with a prompt), on_black (see-through on the glasses), mask, regions (every region coloured: the default with no prompt), json (boxes, areas, scores).

popups.description: Segment an attached picture with SAM 2.1: cut out the thing named in words, at a point or in a box, or (with nothing given) outline every region. Use when the Captain asks to select, mask, isolate or cut out a particular object, or to split a picture into parts.

popups.name: detect_objects

text.description: What to find, in words: "find the mugs and the keyboard".

threshold.description: How sure a box must be (0.4 by default).

output.description: boxes = the picture with labelled boxes (default); json = each label, score and box.

popups.description: Find whatever the words name in an attached picture and box it (Grounding DINO, open vocabulary): "find the mugs". Use when the Captain asks where things are, how many there are, or for bounding boxes.

popups.name: read_document

task.description: text (default): all the words; table: the table as HTML; formula: LaTeX; chart: the chart's data.

output.description: text (default) or json (with the task and length).

popups.description: Read a document, receipt, screenshot, table, formula or chart in an attached picture (PaddleOCR-VL, 100+ languages, mixed scripts): exact text, tables as HTML, formulas as LaTeX. Use for whole documents and tables; a quick glance at a picture doesn't need it.

popups.name: body_pose

output.description: skeleton = the picture with each person's keypoints drawn (default); json = 17 COCO keypoints per person, in pixels, with scores.

popups.description: Body pose of each person in an attached picture (RT-DETR finds people, ViTPose++ places 17 keypoints): a skeleton picture or the keypoints as JSON, for rigging, motion reference and AR anchoring. Use when the Captain asks for pose, keypoints or a skeleton.
